comments.content:
As far I as I know, only pay.ubf.fi will use config but it's also a typescript project so it's not a problem.
YAML standard doesn't define name style - for example Kubernetes/Docker Compose use camelCase in YAML.
@pavlovcik do you agree separating the configs?

Yeah you're right, this will be a problem because internal config uses camelCase and yaml config uses kebab-case, so this will cause trouble in the future too. I think it would be best to stick to one format for both configs - camelCase is natural in JS/TS so I think it should be also used in yaml config. I will make a new issue for this but for now modify `getNewContributorConfig` to read from kebab-case and convert to camelCase manually.
_Originally posted by @whilefoo in https://github.com/ubiquity/ubiquibot/pull/689#discussion_r1314242213_
I think we should change yaml name format to camelCase to avoid having to convert it from kebab-case to camelCase when we parse it. This will also allow to have one unified Typescript type.
On this note I'd like to also discuss the separation of the config into two configs. One config would be EnvConfig which parses env variables and another would be the RepoConfig which parses the yaml. Having one merged config was causing issues in #684 because I had to validate the config and if it's invalid I still needed env variables to create Supabase adapter and create logger to log the error.
@0xcodercrane this might break the bot because it fetches the config from development branch but production bot won't have camelCase yet

you don't need quotes (`"`) when using camelCase
```suggestion
  assistivePricing: false,
```
update this everywhere
